Rashi on Gittin 62b:10:1.hebrew: דלמא בהילך - בהך סיפא לא תיתני "הולך ותן לה" אלא "הילך ותן לה", ד"הילך" ודאי הילך כדקאמרה היא, ואי לאו דאמר "אי אפשי", הוה ליה שליח לקבלה:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:10:1.english: Perhaps [it refers to a case] of "Here you are" - In that latter clause [of the mishna], do not teach "Deliver [it] and give [it] to her," rather "Here you are, and give [it] to her," for "Here you are" certainly [means] "Here it is for you as she said," and were it not that he said "I do not want [you to receive it for her]," he would be an agent for receipt:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:11:1.hebrew: פשיטא איש - זכר יכול ליעשות שליח לבעל להולכה, כיון דאיתרבי שליחות מקרא מושלחה, פשיטא דודאי זכר להולכה רבי:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:11:1.english: It is obvious [that] a man - [i.e.,] a male can become an agent for the husband for delivery [of a bill of divorce]; since agency is derived from the verse, from "and he sends her" [Deut. 24:1], it is obvious that a male was certainly included for delivery:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:11:2.hebrew: שכן בעל - עליו להוליך גט לאשתו, ובמידי דאיהו כשר, שלוחו נמי כשר:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:11:2.english: As a husband - it is [incumbent] upon him to deliver a bill of divorce to his wife, and in a matter for which he [himself] is qualified, his agent is also qualified:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:11:3.hebrew: ואשה - אחרת פשיטא לן דהויא שליח לחברתה לקבלה, מאחר דרבי קרא שליחות לקבלה מ"ושלחה מביתו" — קרי ביה "ושלחה":
Rashi on Gittin 62b:11:3.english: And a woman - [i.e.,] another [woman]: it is obvious to us that she can be an agent for her fellow [woman] for receipt, since the verse included agency for receipt from [the words] "and he sends her [ve-shilchah] from his house" — read it as "and she sends [ve-sholchah] [an agent]."

Rashi on Gittin 62b:11:4.english: As - She herself receives her bill of divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:11:5.hebrew: איפכא מאי - מי אמרי': כיון דהוא עצמו לאו בר קבלה הוא, שאר זכרים נמי לאו בני קבלה נינהו, וכן לענין הולכה באשה:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:11:5.english: What [is the law in] the reverse [case] - Do we say: Since he himself is not subject to receiving [a bill of divorce], other males are also not eligible for receipt, and likewise regarding delivery by a woman?

Rashi on Gittin 62b:12:1.hebrew: בחד שליח - קאמר, דבין א"ל בעל "הולך" בין א"ל "התקבל", הוי שליח להולכה; ואי אמרה ליה איהי מעיקרא לההוא "התקבל", הוי שליח לקבלה. אלמא ההוא דאכשר להיות שליח לבעל להולכה, מכשר להיות שליח לאשה לקבלה:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:12:1.english: [Referring] to one agent - [the Gemara] is saying [that the Mishnah speaks of one and the same agent]: whether the husband said to him "Deliver" or whether he said to him "Receive," he is an agent for delivery; and if she said to that [same agent] initially "Receive," he is an agent for receipt. Thus, the one who is fit to be an agent for the husband for delivery is fit to be an agent for the wife for receipt:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:12:2.hebrew: לא בשני שלוחין - וה"ק: הבעל שאמר לאיש, בין "התקבל" בין "הולך", לשון הולכה היא; והאשה שאמרה לחברתה "התקבל" ונתנו לה הבעל, אם רצה לחזור — לא יחזור, ולאו אשליח דרישא קאי:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:12:2.english: No, [it refers] to two agents - And this is what [the Mishnah] means: [Regarding] a husband who said to a man, whether "Receive [this bill of divorce]" or "Deliver [this bill of divorce]," it is an expression of delivery; and [regarding] a woman who said to her female friend, "Receive [my bill of divorce]," and the husband gave it to her, if [the husband] wishes to retract, he cannot retract — and [this] does not refer to the agent of the first clause:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:13:1.hebrew: והא הכא דחד שליח הוא - לההוא דאמרה ליה איהי "התקבל", א"ל איהו "אי איפשי שתקבל אלא הולך":
Rashi on Gittin 62b:13:1.english: And isn't [the case] here [one] where it is one agent - To that [agent] to whom she said, "Receive [it]," he [the husband] said to him, "I do not want you to receive [it], rather deliver [it]."

Rashi on Gittin 62b:14:1.hebrew: פשוט מינה איש דהוי שליח לקבלה - כלומר, מתרתי בעיין דבעינן לעיל, חדא מצית למפשט מינה; דאיכא למימר מתני' באיש קמיירי, דכשר אף לקבלה. ודין הוא, שהרי מצינו שהוא ראוי לקבלה בגט של בתו קטנה: שהתורה זכתה לו לקבל קידושיה, כדילפינן בכתובות (דף מו:) מ"ויצאה חנם אין כסף", ולקבל את גיטה, דכתיב "ויצאה והיתה לאיש" — איתקש יציאה להויה. הלכך בשליחות נמי כשר; אבל אשה להולכה, אכתי מיבעי לן:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:14:1.english: Resolve from it [that] a man can be an agent for receipt - That is to say: of the two dilemmas that we raised above, one you can resolve from it [the Mishnah]; for one can say [that] the Mishnah is speaking of a man, who is fit even for receipt. And it is logical, for we find that he is fit for receipt with respect to the get of his minor daughter: for the Torah granted him [the right] to accept her betrothal, as we derive in Ketubot (46b) from "and she shall go out free, without money" (Exodus 21:11), and [also] to receive her get, as it is written, "and she goes out and becomes a man's [wife]" (Deuteronomy 24:2) — "going out" [divorce] is juxtaposed to "becoming" [betrothal]. Therefore, in agency as well, he is fit; however, [regarding] a woman for delivery, it is still a dilemma for us:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:14:2.hebrew: אף הנשים כו' - חמותה, ובת חמותה, צרתה, ויבמתה, ובת בעלה:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:14:2.english: Even the women, etc. - Her mother-in-law, her mother-in-law's daughter, her co-wife, her sister-in-law [her husband's brother's wife], and her husband's daughter:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:14:3.english: And there, it is delivery - since [the Mishnah] teaches "to bring":

Rashi on Gittin 62b:15:1.hebrew: ואוקימנא בהולכה - בפרק קמא, מדקתני צריכה לומר "בפני נכתב", והוינן בה: מכי מטא גיטא לידה איגרשה לה? ומתרצינן דאמר לה: "הוי שליח להולכה עד דמטית התם":
Rashi on Gittin 62b:15:1.english: And we established [that she acts as an agent] for delivery - In the first chapter, since [the Mishnah] teaches [that] she must say, "In my presence it was written," and we asked about it: once the get reaches her hand, is she [not already] divorced? And we answered that [the husband] said to her, "Be an agent for delivery until you arrive there."

Rashi on Gittin 62b:16:1.hebrew: ה"ג הבא לי גיטי ואשתך אמרה התקבל לי גיטי - האשה שאמרה לשלוחה: "הבא לי גיטי", והוא אומר לבעל: "אשתך אמרה התקבל לי גיטי":
Rashi on Gittin 62b:16:1.english: Thus we read [the text]: Bring my bill of divorce to me, and your wife said, "Receive my bill of divorce for me" - [This refers to] a woman who said to her agent, "Bring my bill of divorce to me," and he says to the husband, "Your wife said, 'Receive my bill of divorce for me'":

Rashi on Gittin 62b:16:2.hebrew: והוא אומר - הבעל אמר לו: "הילך כמה שאמרה":
Rashi on Gittin 62b:16:2.english: And he says - The husband said to him [the agent], "Here you are, as she said."

Rashi on Gittin 62b:17:1.hebrew: אפי' הגיע גט לידה אינה מגורשת - כדמפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:17:1.english: Even [if] the bill of divorce reached her hand, she is not divorced - As [the Gemara] goes on to explain:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:17:2.hebrew: ש"מ - דמאן דאמר לשליח "הילך כמה שאמרה משלחך", אדיבורא דידיה סמיך; אדעתא דדיבורא דשליח קאמר ליה האי "הילך כמה שאמרה" — דמהימנת לי דשליח לקבלה את. הילכך אינה מגורשת, דכי יהב בעל ניהליה, אדעתא דשליחות קבלה יהיב ניהליה ולאו אדעתא דהולכה, ושליח לקבלה לא הוי. ותפשוט מינה בעיא דאיבעיא לן בב"מ בהשוכר את האומנין — אדיבורא דשליח סמיך:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:17:2.english: Learn from this - that one who says to an agent, "Here [you are], as your sender said," relies on his [the agent's] statement; it is on the basis of the agent's statement that he says to him this "Here [you are], as she said" — [meaning,] "for I trust you that you are an agent for receipt." Therefore she is not divorced, for when the husband gives [the bill of divorce] to him, he gives it to him on the basis of agency for receipt and not on the basis of [agency for] delivery, and he is not an agent for receipt. And from this you may resolve the dilemma that was raised to us in Bava Metzia in [the chapter] HaSokher et HaUmanin — [namely, that] one relies on the statement of the agent:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:17:3.hebrew: דאי אדיבורא דידה סמיך - והכי קאמר ליה: אנא לא ידענא, אלא כדאמרה איהי מסרנא ליה ניהלך:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:17:3.english: For if he relies on her statement - And thus [the husband] says to [the agent]: "I do not know; rather, as she said, I am handing it to you."

Rashi on Gittin 62b:17:4.english: When the bill of divorce reaches her hand, at least let her be divorced - For the husband also appointed him [as] an agent for delivery:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:1:1.english: One who says, "Receive": [If] he seeks to retract - [This refers to] the husband:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:1:2.hebrew: יחזור - דגט חוב הוא לה, ואין חבין לאדם אלא מדעתו, ליעשות לו שליח לחובתו:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:1:2.english: He can retract - Because a bill of divorce is a disadvantage to her, and one may not act to a person's disadvantage except with his knowledge [and consent], [that is,] to become an agent for him to his disadvantage:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:1:3.hebrew: לא יחזור - כיון דאיהי שויתיה שליח, הרי הוא כידה, ונתגרשה מיד בקבלתו של זה:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:1:3.english: He cannot retract - Since she appointed him [as] an agent, he is like her hand, and she is divorced immediately upon this [agent's] receipt [of it]:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:2:1.hebrew: לפיכך - כיון דאמרן אין יכול לחזור, אין לו תקנה לחזור, אא"כ אמר לו הבעל לזה שעשתה אותו שליח לקבלה: "אי אפשי שתקבל לה" להיות כידה, אלא שליח שלי תהא להוליכו לידה:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:2:1.english: Therefore - Since we said [above that] he cannot retract, he has no way to retract unless the husband says to the one whom she appointed [as] an agent for receipt: "I do not want you to receive [it] for her" to be like her [own] hand; rather, you shall be my agent to deliver it to her hand:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:2:2.english: If he wishes to retract - [he may do so] as long as the bill of divorce has not reached her hand:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:2:3.hebrew: יחזור - שאינה מתגרשת אלא מדעת המגרש, והרי אמר: לא יהא גט עד שיגיע גט לידה:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:2:3.english: He can retract - For she is divorced only with the consent of the divorcer, and behold, he said: Let it not be a bill of divorce until the bill of divorce reaches her hand:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:3:1.english: Even [a woman] who says, "Take my bill of divorce for me" - [This] is an expression of receipt:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:4:1.hebrew: טעמא דלא שויתיה שליח לקבלה - א"הולך גט זה לאשתי" קאי, דקתני מתני' "יחזור", ומיירי בדלא שויתיה איהי שליח לקבלה, ובעל לאו בר שוייה שליח לקבלה הוא, דהא חוב הוא לה, והכא הוא דקאמרינן "יחזור":
Rashi on Gittin 62b:4:1.english: The reason is that she did not designate him an agent for receipt - [This] refers to [the clause] "Deliver this bill of divorce to my wife," where the Mishnah teaches "he may retract," and it is dealing with [a case] where she did not designate him an agent for receipt, and the husband is not empowered to designate him an agent for receipt, for it is a disadvantage to her; and it is [specifically] here that we say "he may retract":

Rashi on Gittin 62b:4:2.english: But [if] she appointed him an agent for receipt - and he [the husband] says, "Deliver [it]":

Rashi on Gittin 62b:4:3.english: He cannot retract - because [the husband] did not remove him from her agency:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:4:4.hebrew: אלמא הולך כזכי דמי - ופלוגתא היא בפ"ק (לעיל גיטין דף יד.):
Rashi on Gittin 62b:4:4.english: Thus, "deliver" is like "acquire" - And it is a dispute in the first chapter (above, Gittin 14a):

Rashi on Gittin 62b:5:1.hebrew: לא לעולם לאו כזכי דמי - ואפילו שויתיה איהי שליח לקבלה, ואמר לו איהו "הולך", מיעקר עקריה משליחותא ושוייה איהו שליח להולכה; והאי דנקט מתני' בדלא שויתיה שליח, משום "התקבל" נקט לה, ד"התקבל" איצטריכא ליה לאשמועי': דאע"ג דלא שויתיה היא שליח, ובעל נמי לאו בר שוייה שליח לקבלה הוא אלא להולכה, ואיהו לא אמר "הולך", אפ"ה כי מטא גט לידה מיהא, מגורשת:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:5:1.english: No, actually [saying "Deliver"] is not like "Acquire" - And even if she appointed him an agent for receipt, and he [the husband] said to him, "Deliver," he has completely uprooted him from [her] agency and appointed him an agent for delivery. And that which the Mishnah taught [a case] where she did not appoint him an agent, it taught it on account of "Receive," for it was necessary for [the Tanna] to teach us [the case of] "Receive": that even though she did not appoint him an agent, and the husband too is not able to appoint an agent for receipt, but only for delivery, and he did not say "Deliver," nevertheless, when the bill of divorce reaches her hand, at any rate, she is divorced.

Rashi on Gittin 62b:6:1.hebrew: לא ליהוי גיטא - דהא לאו להולכה שוייה שליח, ולקבלה נמי לא בר שוייה שליח הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:6:1.english: It would not be a [valid] bill of divorce - For he did not appoint him [as] an agent for delivery, and for receipt as well, he is not eligible to appoint him [as] an agent:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:6:2.hebrew: קמ"ל - ד"התקבל" דקאמר ליה, "התקבל והולך" קאמר, דאדם יודע שאין לו שליחות לקבלה; ואיידי דתנא "התקבל", תנא "הולך", דהכי קאמר מתני': בין שאמר בעל בלשון קבלה, בין שאמר בלשון הולכה — הוי שליח להולכה:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:6:2.english: It teaches us - that [when] he [the husband] says to him [the agent], "Receive," he means "Receive and deliver," because a person knows that he [a husband] does not have [the power to appoint] agency for receipt; and since it taught "Receive," it [also] taught "deliver," for this is what the Mishnah is saying: Whether the husband spoke in the language of receipt or spoke in the language of delivery, he is an agent for delivery:

Rashi on Gittin 62b:7:1.hebrew: מאי לאו - אתרוייהו מילי דתנא לעיל מינה קאי: לא שנא כי אמר הבעל קבלה ולא שנא הולכה, אי שויתיה איהי שליח לקבלה מעיקרא, לא יחזור; ש"מ הולך כזכי דמי:
Rashi on Gittin 62b:7:1.english: What, is it not - [This] refers to both matters that were taught above it: whether the husband said [an expression of] receipt or whether [he said an expression of] delivery, if she appointed him an agent for receipt from the outset, he cannot retract; learn from this [that saying] "deliver" is like [saying] "acquire":

Tosafot on Gittin 62b:10:1.hebrew: דילמא בהילך - אינו מגיה, אלא כלומר: דילמא איכא דתני הילך:
Tosafot on Gittin 62b:10:1.english: Perhaps with heilakh [here you are] - [The Gemara] is not emending [the Mishnah's text]; rather, it means to say: perhaps there is [a Tanna] who teaches heilakh:

Tosafot on Gittin 62b:11:1.hebrew: איש לקבלה ואשה להולכה מאי - משום דבגט, אשה בהולכה לא שייכא, ואיש בקבלה לא שייך, משום הכי קבעי:
Tosafot on Gittin 62b:11:1.english: A man for receipt and a woman for delivery, what [is the halakha] - Because with a bill of divorce, a woman is not involved in delivery, and a man [is not involved] in receipt — therefore [the Gemara] asks:

Tosafot on Gittin 62b:1:1.hebrew: האומר התקבל - בירושלמי תנא "התקבל" אחר "הניזקין", ואחריו "מי שאחזו". וכן נראה לר"ת, ד"הניזקין" תנא בתר "השולח", משום דאיירי במילי דהויא מפני תיקון העולם, והשתא הדר למילתיה דאיירי בשליחות; ואיידי דאיירי באומר לשנים "תנו", או לשלשה "כתבו ותנו", תנא בתריה "מי שאחזו" דאיירי נמי באומר "כתבו"; ואיידי דתנא ב"מי שאחזו" במגורשת ואינה מגורשת, תנא בתריה "הזורק" דקתני בה: מחצה על מחצה מגורשת ואינה מגורשת:
Tosafot on Gittin 62b:1:1.english: One who says: "Receive" - In the Jerusalem Talmud, [the chapter] Hitkabbel is taught after HaNizakin, and after it Mi SheAchazo. And so it seems [correct] to Rabbeinu Tam: for HaNizakin is taught after HaSholeach because it deals with matters that are for the betterment of the world, and now [the Tanna] returns to his [previous] subject, which deals with agency; and since [this chapter] deals with one who says to two [people], "Give," or to three [people], "Write and give," he taught after it Mi SheAchazo, which also deals with one who says, "Write"; and since in Mi SheAchazo he taught about [a woman who is] divorced and not divorced, he taught after it HaZorek, in which it is taught: "[If it is] half and half, she is divorced and not divorced":

Tosafot on Gittin 62b:4:1.hebrew: הא שויתיה שליח - השתא סלקא דעתין דלא איצטריך למיתני "התקבל", אלא למידק דכי היכי ד"התקבל" דוקא בלא שויתיה שליח, "הולך" נמי דוקא בלא שויתיה שליח:
Tosafot on Gittin 62b:4:1.english: But [where] she designated him an agent - At this point [the Gemara] assumes that it was not necessary [for the Mishnah] to teach "Receive," except to infer that just as "Receive" [applies] specifically where she did not designate him an agent, "Deliver" also [applies] specifically where she did not designate him an agent:
